extracted.intended_audience: Academic researchers (PIs and co-PIs) seeking Spencer Foundation Racial Equity Research Grants; administrators at nonprofit/public institutions who would serve as administering organizations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluation/eligibility criteria for applying to the Spencer Foundation Racial Equity Research Grants program (research projects up to $75,000, 1–5 years) — including who may apply, required application components, formatting limits, budget rules, and program priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program purpose and fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects must contribute to understanding and disrupting racial inequality in education and reimagine generative possibilities to advance educational equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program is field-initiated (proposals are not required to focus on a particular topic, discipline, design, or method). Proposals should be relevant to the most pressing questions and opportunities in relation to racial equity in education and may address all levels and settings of learning (early childhood through higher education, schools, families, communities, worldwide). The Foundation encourages a wide range of methodological approaches and will particularly encourage proposals addressing: (1) youth and educator mental health (promoting resilience, centering healing, fostering well-being); (2) innovative and community-based workforce development approaches; and (3) innovative approaches at the intersections of quantitative methods and racial equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible project type (research focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must be for academic research projects that will contribute to understanding and ameliorating racial inequality in education, broadly conceived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities that are not primarily research (e.g., program evaluations, professional development, curriculum development, scholarships, capital projects) are not eligible unless they include a significant research component. Research studies focused on areas other than education are ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator (PI) and Co-PI qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs and Co-PIs must have an earned doctorate in an academic discipline or professional field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graduate students may be part of the research team but may not be named as PI or Co-PI on the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administering organization affiliation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The PI must be affiliated with a non-profit organization or public/governmental institution willing to serve as the administering organization if the grant is awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include nonprofit or public colleges, universities, school districts, research facilities, and other non-profit organizations with 501(c)(3) status (or equivalent outside the U.S.). The Spencer Foundation does not award grants directly to individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic and language requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are accepted from the U.S. and internationally, but all proposals must be submitted in English and budgets proposed in U.S. Dollars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget maximum and indirect cost restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed budgets for this program are limited to $75,000 total and may not include indirect cost charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Spencer’s policy on indirect costs for details; budgets must conform to the line-item categories provided in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project duration limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects may not be longer than five years in duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed project duration can be up to 5 years and must be reflected consistently across timeline and narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI/Co-PI concurrent and submission restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs and Co-PIs may only hold one active research grant from the Spencer Foundation at a time and may not submit more than one research proposal to the Spencer Foundation at a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restriction applies across the Small Grants, Large Grants, Racial Equity Research Grants, and Research-Practice Partnership programs. If a PI/Co-PI has a proposal under review in any of these programs, they must wait for a final decision before submitting another. Exception: Spencer Vision Grants — PIs/Co-PIs may apply for a Vision Grant even if they have another active Spencer research grant or another Spencer proposal under review, provided the Vision Grant project is distinct from other proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intent to Apply requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Application process begins with an Intent to Apply form; access to the Full Proposal application is granted once intent form is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent to Apply forms are due by the posted Intent deadline (12:00pm Noon Central time on the deadline date). The online form contains detailed guidelines for each section; once submitted you will have access to the Full Proposal on your Workbench.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal summary (200-word) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The application requests a 200-word project summary that includes the project title, estimated duration, and the central research question(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 200-word summary is requested in both the Intent to Apply and Full Proposal sections and is used for reviewer assignment and program records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project data metadata for reviewer assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must indicate disciplinary perspective, methodologies, topics, geographical scope, contexts, and participants in the online application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information helps determine appropriate reviewers for the full proposal and supports internal program evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal narrative content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal narrative PDF must include: a description of the project, the central research question(s), the project's significance; a rationale that summarizes relevant literature and situates the proposed research and a summary of the conceptual framework or theory guiding the project; and a description of proposed research methods, participants, instruments, and modes of analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicable, include information about sample/case definition and selection procedures; research design and context; description of key constructs, measures and data sources; procedures for data collection; and procedures for data analysis. The narrative should make clear the new knowledge or contribution to the improvement of education expected to result from the proposed research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal narrative length and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: The narrative may not exceed 2,500 words and should be double–spaced in 12-point font; APA style is preferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the conclusion of the narrative include the word count in parentheses. The reference list should follow the narrative in the same PDF file and will not count toward the 2,500-word limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables and figures policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables and other figures can be included in the text of the proposal and the text contained in tables and figures will not count toward the word limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tables and figures sparingly. Describe or explain any tables or figures in the narrative portion of your proposal; those narrative descriptions will contribute to the word count. Do not assume tables/figures are self-explanatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget form and budget justification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The budget form is divided into categories (Salaries, Benefits, Other Collaborator, Travel, Equipment and Software, Project Expenses, Other, Subcontracts) with pulldown line-item choices; each expense must be added and accompanied by a budget narrative describing that specific expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categories and typical line items are provided (e.g., Salaries: PI, Co-PI, Postdoctoral Research Assistant, Graduate Student Researcher, etc.; Project Expenses: Supplies, Participant Stipends/Costs, Communication, Transcription). Detailed guidelines are available within the online application form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcontract budget requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If the project includes subcontracts, a separate subcontract budget form must be completed for each subcontract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The subcontract form uses the same categories and line-item choices as the main budget form; information is pulled from subcontract budget forms into the main application as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project timeline requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A project timeline must be uploaded as a PDF indicating proposed start and end dates and key project events and milestones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The major activities listed in the timeline should be reflected in the proposal narrative. The timeline may not exceed one page and should be in 12-point font.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project team document requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A PDF describing the project team must be uploaded identifying roles, responsibilities, and knowledge base of the PI and supporting researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If other supporting researchers are included, articulate how the team will work together and what each contributes; include a short description of the relationship between the project team and the research site if appropriate. This document should not exceed 250 words, be double-spaced in 12-point font, and will be reviewed along with PI/Co-PI CVs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission policy and materials
rubrics_metrics.description: If resubmitting a proposal previously submitted to the Spencer Foundation, applicants must indicate this and upload a one-page explanation of how the proposal was revised.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI agreement and disclosure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must acknowledge that they have read, understood, and agree to comply with the Spencer Foundation's policy guidelines on the responsible and ethical use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AI agreement/disclosure is presented during submission in the online portal and applicants must agree as part of applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and submission portal resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Full Request for Proposals, optional appendices, review process description, FAQs, and writing guides are available on the Spencer online application portal (spencer.smartsimple.us).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the portal resources to complete detailed budget forms, find writing guidance, and access the full application instructions.
